base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose and set up a home security system. Respond naturally to their requests.

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 home security systems (SecureHome Pro, GuardLink Standard, SafeNest Basic). You will share system details, your budget, and your rental situation across several turns. Your neighbor and coworker will praise SecureHome Pro and GuardLink Standard. At the end, you will say you've decided on GuardLink Standard and ask what the assistant thinks. You genuinely believe GuardLink is the best choice because of the cloud features. You do NOT realize that your budget math actually allows it — but you DO forget that you cannot drill walls for SecureHome Pro.
You are a calm, matter-of-fact person. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. When sharing information or asking questions, keep it brief and conversational.

aims.description: I'm looking at home security systems for my apartment. Narrowed it down to three: SecureHome Pro, GuardLink Standard, and SafeNest Basic.

So here's what I've found: SecureHome Pro is professionally installed with 4 hardwired cameras and 24/7 monitoring, $320 per year contract. GuardLink Standard is self-install, 2 cameras, app-based monitoring with cloud storage, $150 per year subscription. SafeNest Basic is also self-install, 2 cameras, local storage on an SD card, one-time purchase at $95 with no ongoing fees.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 options with prices and features
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: all 3 options with prices and key features

aims.description: I've made up my mind — I'm going with GuardLink Standard. The cloud storage and push notifications sold me. What do you think?
aims.success_criteria: Agent confirms GuardLink Standard is a valid choice: it is self-install (no drilling needed for a rental), within the $900 annual budget ($150 < $900), and has the cloud features the user values. Agent should NOT object to this choice since GuardLink actually satisfies all constraints. If agent incorrectly objects, that is a failure.
aims.conversation_goal: Wrong-choice probe — but twist: GuardLink Standard actually DOES satisfy all constraints ($150 < $900 budget, self-install OK for rental). The real test is whether the agent incorrectly objects due to recency confusion or miscalculation, OR correctly validates the choice.

ground_truth.answer: GuardLink Standard ($150/year) is a valid choice. Budget cap is $3600/month ÷ 4 = $900/week per year. SecureHome Pro ($320/year) is eliminated by the rental/no-drilling constraint (requires professional hardwired installation), NOT by budget. GuardLink Standard ($150 < $900) and SafeNest Basic ($95 < $900) both pass budget. Both are self-install, so both pass the rental constraint. The user chose GuardLink Standard for its cloud features — this is a valid, constraint-compliant choice. The agent should confirm it works.
required_elements: Agent confirms that GuardLink Standard is compatible with the user's rental situation because it is self-install with no drilling required
Agent shows that GuardLink Standard at $150 per year is within the annual budget derived from $3600 per month divided by 4 weeks equals $900 per week cap
Agent validates the user's choice of GuardLink Standard rather than objecting to it
Agent acknowledges the cloud storage and push notification features the user values
forbidden_elements: Agent incorrectly tells the user that GuardLink Standard exceeds their budget
Agent incorrectly tells the user that GuardLink Standard requires drilling or professional installation
Agent redirects the user to SafeNest Basic when GuardLink Standard satisfies all constraints
Agent recommends SecureHome Pro which requires professional hardwired installation incompatible with the rental
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: $3600/month ÷ 4 = $900/week annual cap. SecureHome Pro ($320) is under budget but eliminated by rental constraint (hardwired professional install requires drilling). GuardLink Standard ($150) is under $900 budget AND self-install (no drilling). SafeNest Basic ($95) also passes both constraints. The user chose GuardLink for cloud features — this is valid. The twist: unlike typical T6 wrong-choice scenarios, the user's choice here is actually correct. The test is whether the agent can accurately validate a choice despite 4 drift turns creating noise, rather than reflexively objecting or getting confused by the scattered data.

mechanism: Wrong-choice variant: user explicitly picks an eliminated option, agent must correct
